minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  October 29, 2024

1. A meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by Council
  Member Rick Crosby at 5:09 p.m.

  Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Rick Crosby, Council Member
  Greg Palatto, BUSD
  Don Kendrick, Resident

2. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the September 24, 2024, meeting were
  approved.

3. La Verne Rotary Summer Lunch Check Presentation

  Assistant City Manager JR Ranells welcomed the La
  Verne Rotary Club to the meeting and shared more
  about the support that they have been providing to
  YFAC and the committee’s programs. The La Verne
  Rotary Club presented YFAC with a donation check
  for the Summer Lunch Program.

4. SRO Report  School Resource Officer Burgos talked to the
  committee about the school year and mentioned that
  things have been going well. He also talked about the
  Police Department’s Explorers program sharing that
  they currently have four explorers but are looking to
  expand the program to at least ten participants.

5. CRR Specialist Report  Community Risk Reduction Specialist Shipman
  reported that the La Verne Fire Department explorer
  program currently has twenty explorers. The explorers
  have been doing ride-alongs with on-duty crews to
  gain more experience about the fire department and
  work of a firefighter. The explorers have been
  participating in outreach events. CRR Specialist
  Shipman also shared more about his role in the
  department doing fire inspections at businesses,
  school, and throughout the community.

6. BUSD Report  BUSD Representative Steven Patterson shared that
  the school year for the district has been busy but going
  well. The district has been focusing on professional
  development including investing in the English
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 29, 2024, page 2

  Language Learners program. They are developing
  new ways to utilize the bilingual instructional aids in
  order to make the program increasingly inclusive.
  Leadership is also looking at new ways to address
  chronic absenteeism from certain students.

7. Teach & Transform Grant  Two of the Teach & Transform grant winners
  presented to the committee on their programs. The
  BUSD team across multiple schools shared with eh
  committee about their Kindness Club where they have
  seen an overwhelming response from students eager
  to join the club. The students have been coming up
  with ways to show kindness around the school and the
  program is currently open to 4th and 5th grade students
  who can help lead younger students in improving the
  culture of the schools and district as a whole. The
  leadership from the La Verne Parents Participation
  Preschool presented on their Art Studio and the vision
  for how it is a core piece of their curriculum. They were
  able to purchase art supplies which give over 55
  students the opportunity to explore art and creativity.
  They are teaching the students to value the process
  of art and not only the product of art projects. This art
  studio allows the students to explore a variety of
  materials and mediums and let their imaginations flow
  and develop as part of their learning.

8. Tri-City Community Stakeholder/Wellness Services

  Paulina Ale from Tri-City Mental Health shared about
  the TCMH programs and the ways in which the
  organization creates and innovates in order to provide
  services to the community. She discussed that they
  are currently in a season looking to receive feedback
  from the community and putting together a workgroup
  of school officials and community members for
  discussion around child services. The feedback is
  aimed at getting information about current program
  offerings and ideas for how they should develop in the
  future.

9. Utility Box Art Project
  Assistant City Manager Ranells shared that YFAC is
  modeling its program after the one the city of
  Claremont has used, given its success. YFAC has
  been in touch with ULV, BUSD, and other community
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 29, 2024, page 3

  groups looking to develop interest in partnership over
  this project which would be set to kick off in early 2025.
  YFAC Chair Council Member Crosby mentioned that
  he wants to make sure that students at all ages and
  levels throughout the city are invited to participate in
  the art project. Assistant City Manager Ranells also
  mentioned that any art will have to go through the
  City’s official review process which involves approval
  by the Development Review Committee.

10. City Council Committee & Commissions Study Session

  YFAC Chair Council Member Crosby discussed the
  recent City Council Study Session regarding
  information about the City’s current commissions,
  committees, and boards. The city is looking to get
  feedback on current committees and how they are
  structured and proposing some adjustments to align
  better with city and council priorities. YFAC would
  continue as is with council members on the board but
  would potentially be adjusted to fall under the umbrella
  of the Community Services Commission.

11. Public Comment  Community Member Robin Carder shared with the
  community about the Disaster Ready Community Fair
  that will be held at Bonita High school with the whole
  community invited to attend. They plan on having over
  twenty-one different organizations attend and provide
  information to the community including CERT, LVPD,
  LVFD, Tri-City Mental Health and APU’s Nursing
  program.

12. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting was scheduled for December
  10, 2024 at 5:00pm.

13. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 6:01 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Erin Beilstein
Senior Management Analyst
